title: Fauci Pleads the Fifth

desc: Sen. Josh Hawley grills Dr. Fauci in a Senate hearing — asking what day of the week it is, what color tie he's wearing — and gets the Fifth Amendment every time. 111 invocations, zero answers.

title: France Student Protests: Tear Gas in Paris as Hundreds of Thousands March
hook: “They don't really care about us” — students, teachers and parents flood the streets of Paris.
desc: France's student protest wave peaks on October 6 with a national day of demonstrations: 256,000 marchers counted by the Interior Ministry, 450,000 by organizers, up to 100,000 in Paris marching from République to Nation. What began September 21 at a Créteil high school over teacher shortages, overcrowded classes and crumbling buildings has spread nationwide — 24 schools burned or ransacked, 78 staff injured, over 6,500 arrested, mostly minors. Police fired tear gas as the Paris march ended; Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu suspended classes through the week.

title: US Pulls B-1 Bombers From UK Base Over Iran Threat
hook: “They didn't fly out by accident… there was a threat.”
desc: Washington pulled about a dozen B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in England over the weekend after intelligence pointed to an Iran-linked threat against the base. The move followed the September 27 arrest of five British men near the base over a suspected terror plot — with a seventh arrest in London on Tuesday — and the UK prime minister cited ‘strong indications’ of Iranian involvement, which Tehran denies. President Trump confirmed the bombers ‘didn't fly out by accident,’ contradicting Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who had called it a ‘regular rotation.’ Vice President JD Vance said it was done ‘out of an abundance of caution.’ Fairford is the only European airfield for US heavy bombers and was used in this year's strikes on Iran.

title: Flávio Bolsonaro Stuns Lula, Forces Brazil Runoff
hook: Polls said Lula would win the first round. They were wrong.
desc: Brazil is heading to a presidential runoff on October 25 after Flávio Bolsonaro — the 45-year-old son of jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro — stunned the polls by finishing first with 47.03% of the vote, ahead of incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's 45.16%. Lula, 80, admitted he was ‘convinced’ he would win outright in the first round. The 2.2-million-vote gap is one of the narrowest in recent Brazilian history, and the two frontrunners took 92% of all votes — the most polarized first round since democracy returned in 1985.
tags: Brazil Bolsonaro Lula election runoff Latin America
text: Brazil is heading to a presidential runoff after the top two finishers in Sunday's election were unable to secure enough votes for an outright victory. In combat, Luis Enazio Lula de Silva will face Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is currently serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election. The runoff is set for the 25th of October.
